title: The hiking trail had a new sign this year. It says you are being followed. It's correct.
transcript:
The hiking trail had a new sign this year. It says you are being followed. It's correct. The sign was hand-painted, nailed to a pine at the second switchback. WARNING. Stay on the trail. Do not wave back.

My sister Kate laughed and took a picture. We kept going. It was a clear afternoon, the kind of day where nothing could go wrong.

An hour later, we saw someone far up the ridge, standing at the edge of the trees. Waving, slowly, with both arms.

Kate waved back. I told her not to, but she was already doing it.

After that, we heard footsteps behind us. Always a little behind, matching our pace. When we stopped, they stopped one half-second late.

At the lake, we turned to look. Nobody was on the trail. But a line of wet footprints came out of the water and stopped right behind Kate.

She went pale. She asked me quietly, "Why is your shadow longer than mine?"

I looked down. Mine was normal. Hers had two heads.

We ran. I don't remember much, only that the sign was gone when we passed the switchback, and that Kate wouldn't stop waving at the trees.

She still does it from her window.

Sometimes, something waves back.
